lines: STAT 110 · Reasoning with Data
Meridian State University · Fall 2026 · 3 credits · 15 weeks (Aug 24 – Dec 11)
Instructor: Dr. Amara Okafor · a.okafor@meridianstate.example · Office hours Tue 2–4 pm, Hale 214
Meets Tuesday and Thursday, 9:30–10:45 (75 min), Hale 110. Prerequisite: none. 100-level.
Course description
An introduction to reasoning with data for students who will read statistics far more often than they
compute them. We ask statistical questions, collect and describe data, compare groups, and judge
claims made in public.
Required text
OpenIntro Statistics, 4th edition (free online).

sections.text: Learning outcomes By the end of the course you will be able to: 1. Tell a statistical question from a non-statistical one. 2. Understand variability in data. 3. Describe the center and spread of a distribution. 4. Design a simple study to answer a question. 5. Communicate findings to a non-technical audience. 6. Critique a statistical claim in the news.

sections.text: Course policies Attendance: attend both weekly meetings; more than three unexcused absences lowers the participation grade. Late work: 10% per day, up to five days. No late quizzes. Academic integrity: the Meridian State honor code applies to all work. Generative AI: you may use AI tools to check your reasoning; you may not submit AI-written text as your own. Cite any AI use. Accommodations: contact Accessibility Services in the first two weeks to arrange accommodations.
